holidays.name: National Eat a Red Apple Day
holidays.description: A crisp celebration of the humble red apple, urging everyone to crunch into a shiny red one and feel like Snow White (minus the poison, hopefully).
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that appears on American food holiday calendars. Its exact creator is unknown, but it fits the tradition of celebrating produce at peak harvest season.
holidays.funFact: Apples belong to the rose family, and a ripe apple floats in water because about 25 percent of its volume is air.

holidays.name: World AIDS Day
holidays.description: An international day of awareness, remembrance, and support for people living with HIV and those lost to AIDS. It is not a quirky holiday, but it is the very first global health day ever created, and its red ribbon is recognized worldwide.
holidays.origin: Founded in 1988 by James W. Bunn and Thomas Netter, two public information officers at the World Health Organization, and it has been observed every December 1 since.
holidays.funFact: World AIDS Day was the first-ever global health day, paving the way for other awareness days like World Cancer Day.

holidays.name: Rosa Parks Day
holidays.description: A day honoring Rosa Parks, the civil rights icon whose refusal to give up her bus seat helped spark the Montgomery Bus Boycott.
holidays.origin: It commemorates December 1, 1955, when Parks was arrested in Montgomery, Alabama. California and Missouri observe it officially, and Ohio and Oregon observe it on different dates.
holidays.funFact: The Montgomery Bus Boycott that followed lasted 381 days and ended with a Supreme Court ruling against bus segregation.

holidays.name: Day Without Art
holidays.description: A somber and creative day when galleries, museums, and arts organizations cover artwork, dim lights, or close to reflect on the impact of AIDS on the arts community.
holidays.origin: It began in 1989, organized by the group Visual AIDS, as a response to the many artists lost to the epidemic.
holidays.funFact: Some museums mark the day by draping famous artworks in black cloth, so the absence of art makes a statement of its own.

holidays.name: Christmas Lights Day (Start of Advent Calendar Season)
holidays.description: December 1 is when millions of people pop open the first little door of their advent calendars, with treats ranging from chocolate to cheese, beer, and even tiny toys.
holidays.origin: Advent calendars originated in 19th-century Germany, where Protestant families marked the days before Christmas, sometimes by lighting candles or drawing chalk lines on doors.
holidays.funFact: The first printed advent calendar is often credited to Gerhard Lang, who produced one in Munich in the early 1900s, inspired by a calendar his mother made for him.
